text: Under the Azure SQL umbrella sit three genuinely different products: Azure SQL Database (single fully-managed database), Azure SQL Managed Instance (fully-managed instance, near-full surface), and SQL Server on an Azure VM (full IaaS, 100% surface).

Azure SQL Database is most PaaS — database-scoped, fastest to provision, least to manage. Managed Instance gives near-100% SQL Server surface, including Agent and cross-database queries, while Microsoft still patches and backs it up. SQL Server on a VM is the real binary, full surface, but you own the OS again.
Need just a database, fast and low-maintenance? Azure SQL Database. Need Agent jobs or linked servers but still want PaaS patching? Managed Instance. Need the OS itself? SQL Server on a VM.
This is a first pass — Chapter 3 revisits the same decision against real business requirements. Next up: applying the IaaS/PaaS lens directly to these three options.
